blocks.text: Privileged credentials streamline access to privileged consoles by mapping authentication details to a privileged credentials policy. Based on the privileged credentials policy, credentials are automatically injected into the privileged console without having to manually add them.

Credentials can be discovered from external identity sources (e.g., Active Directory (AD) or Entra ID) or created locally within the Zscaler Admin Console. Discovered credentials can be moved into a managed state, where Zscaler automatically rotates the passwords. These managed privileged credentials can be used in future sessions. A credential class policy can be applied to managed privileged credentials to control rotation behavior (i.e., 30-day rotation, after each use, or never rotate). You can create privileged credential pools to group and organize existing privileged credentials.
Privileged credentials provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: Allow controlled access to users (e.g., third-party vendors, contractors, etc.) by using a privileged console with privileged credentials.
Provide secure seamless access to privileged consoles in a controlled environment.

blocks.text: To use a privileged credential, you must first create a privileged portal and a privileged console. The privileged portal and privileged console are then assigned to the privileged credential. To discover credentials from an AD or Entra ID, you must deploy a credential agent within your infrastructure.
To learn more about PRA, see Understanding Privileged Remote Access. To set up PRA, see Step-by-Step Configuration Guide for Privileged Remote Access.

blocks.heading: About the Managed Privileged Credentials Page

blocks.text: On the Managed page (Zero Trust Browser > Credentials Management > Privileged Credentials > Managed), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Add a new privileged credential.
Discover credentials from the AD.
Click the Filter icon to display or hide the filters.
Click the Search icon to locate specific information in the table.

Filter the information that appears in the table. By default, no filters are applied. You can also save applied filters to your preferences so that they're visible in future user sessions. To learn more, see Using Tables.

If you are using a Microtenant, then the Microtenant Ownership Type filter is available. By default, the Configured within Microtenant filter option is applied to show the privileged credentials configured within that specific Microtenant. The options for the filter are based on access type (Global and Configured within Microtenant). The Global option filters the information in the table that is configured within the Default Microtenant. The only available operator for this filter type is Equals.
Refresh the Managed page to reflect the most current information.
View a list of all privileged credentials that are configured. Both local and discovered privileged credentials are displayed. For each privileged credential, you can see:
Name: The name of the privileged credential.
Status: The rotation status of the privileged credential.
Available: Discovered privileged credentials that are available to be used.
Local: Locally created privileged credentials that can be used.
Rotation Failed: Discovered privileged credentials with a failed rotation.
Class: The rotation schedule assigned to the privileged credential.
Last Rotation: The date, time, and time zone that the privileged credential last rotated.
Next Rotation: The date, time, and time zone that the privileged credential rotates next.
Updated: The date, time, and time zone that the privileged credential was updated.

blocks.text: Privileged credentials that are created in the Default Microtenant are inherited across Microtenants.

blocks.item: Rotate the privileged credential in real time.
Edit a privileged credential.

blocks.text: If the credentials are changed after you created and saved the privileged credential, you must update the new credential details (e.g., Username, Password, Private Key) to continue using the privileged credential.

blocks.item: Select to view additional actions, including deleting a privileged credential and moving the privileged credential into a Microtenant.

blocks.text: If privileged credential policies are associated with the privileged credential, then the policies must be deleted to move the privileged credential to a different Microtenant.

blocks.item: Modify the columns displayed in the table.
Display more rows or a different page of the table.
Go to the Discovered page to manage credentials discovered from the AD.
Go to the Ignored page to manage credentials that have been designated as ignored from the AD.
